context: Given a positive integer n (n ≥ 2), write it as the sum of m positive integers (m ≥ 2), n = n₁ + n₂ + … + nₘ. The goal is to maximize the product of the m pieces, n₁ × n₂ × … × nₘ.
description: A gray bar at the top represents the total length n. Below it, vertical dashed lines divide a colored bar of the same length into pieces labeled from left to right n₁, n₂, n₃, …, nₘ₋₂, nₘ₋₁, and nₘ. Dashed lines align the ends of the two bars, showing that the pieces still add up to n. The objective below reads “Given an integer n, find max(n₁ × n₂ × n₃ × … × nₘ₋₂ × nₘ₋₁ × nₘ).”

frames.explanation: The labels and ellipsis stand for any number m of pieces. The drawing does not require at least six pieces: m can be as small as 2. It gives no numerical values for n, m, or the pieces, so the drawn widths do not give their sizes.
frames.title: Defining the maximum product after cutting

summary: With the sum fixed, choose the number and sizes of the pieces to maximize their product.
title: Defining the maximum product after cutting
